rounds.text: Remsons Industries Ltd trades at an attractive valuation relative to its peers, with an EV/EBITDA of 6.53x against a sector benchmark of 12.91x and a P/E of 13.27x compared to its sector average of 25.2x [E6, E11]. Fundamentals are outpacing the stock price, evidenced by a 10-year compounded profit growth of 40% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 19%, while the share price fell 39% over the past year [E18, E21, E25, E56]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis estimates an intrinsic value of Rs 141 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 44.2% against the current market price of Rs 78.6 [E2, E45, E46]. Operational performance is robust, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of 1.50x, operating cash flow of Rs 18 Cr, and completely cleared capital work in progress at Rs 0 Cr indicating that new capacity is ready to come online [E34, E35, E40]. Institutional participation is building with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes since September 2023 alongside positive money flow [E42, E43, E44], supported by a supportive sector tailwind in Automobile & Auto Components [E69, E71]. Conceded: Promoter holding has decreased to 62.83% from 75.00% [E41], and the stock sits near its 52-week low with a relative-strength rating of 0 [E5, E51].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 13.27x and EV/EBITDA of 6.53x below sector benchmarks [E6, E11], and DCF models indicate an intrinsic value of Rs 141 [E45]. However, the bull's valuation discount is offset by weak historical profitability, evidenced by a low return on equity of 10.6% over the last 3 years and a median ROE of 12% over 10 years [E26, E61]. Furthermore, the bull's claim of robust operational momentum ignores mediocre sales expansion, which is flagged for poor compounded growth of 11.1% over the past five years and slowing 3-year growth of 8% [E16, E60]. While the bull highlights cleared capital work in progress [E40], this coincides with rising debt burdens, as borrowings increased to Rs 78 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 69 Cr a year earlier [E39]. Conceded: institutional holdings show slight increases [E42, E43], but this is undermined by a significant promoter sell-down from 75.00% to 62.83% [E41]. Finally, the bull's dismissal of price action is dangerous given an extreme relative-strength rating of 0, positioning the stock near its 52-week low with heavy annualised volatility of 64.7% [E5, E48, E51, E54].
